hints: Start by recalling how a bacterial cell is fundamentally different from an animal or plant cell in terms of internal membranes.
Think about the boundary layers around the cell and the genetic material free in the cytoplasm.
Remember the very small structures for protein synthesis and the fluid interior, plus any extra small circles of DNA.
Check your drawing would lose marks if you add a nucleus, mitochondria, ER or large vacuole, and make sure each structure has a clear label line.
walkthrough:
Remember What Makes a Bacterium Prokaryotic**
You are drawing Vibrio cholerae, so think prokaryote, not eukaryote. That means no true nucleus with envelope, no mitochondria, no ER, no Golgi, no large vacuole. If you draw any of those you limit your marks, so keep the inside simple.

Add the Boundaries and Interior**
Draw two boundary lines: an outer cell wall made of peptidoglycan / murein for strength, and an inner cell surface membrane. Fill the interior with cytoplasm / cytosol containing small dots for 70S ribosomes for protein synthesis.

Add the Genetic Material Correctly**
Draw one larger tangled circle or loop labelled DNA / bacterial chromosome / nucleoid, free in the cytoplasm with no membrane around it and no histones. Then draw one or more much smaller circles labelled plasmid. Keep plasmids clearly smaller than the main DNA.

Final answer: Draw inside outline: cell wall outer layer, cell surface membrane just inside wall, circular DNA / nucleoid tangled in cytoplasm, 70S ribosomes as dots, cytoplasm / cytosol, small circular plasmid(s). No membrane-bound organelles drawn.

hints: Look back at the definition given: proportion of cases that result in death. Which two numbers from 2015 will you use and how do you turn a proportion into a %?
walkthrough:
Apply the Formula**
Case fatality rate is deaths divided by cases times 100. So $\frac{1304}{172454} \times 100 = 0.756...\%$. Rounded to the nearest 0.1% this is $0.8\%$, which is below the 1% expected with proper treatment.

hints: A rate above 5% when proper treatment gives below 1% suggests treatment is late, missing or not working - what stages of care could fail?
Think about two separate reasons: problems with getting diagnosis and rehydration or antibiotics to patients, versus problems inside patients or bacteria that make treatment less effective.
walkthrough:
Link High Death Rate to Treatment Failure**
Cholera kills by severe water loss. With prompt oral rehydration therapy and antibiotics the rate should be under 1%. A rate over 5% means many patients are not getting effective care in time.

Suggest Two Distinct Causes**
One explanation could be delay or lack of diagnosis and treatment, for example no supply of ORS, no clean water to mix it, or belief in other remedies. A second different explanation could be lack of effective antibiotics, antibiotic-resistant strains of V. cholerae, or patients already malnourished or immunocompromised so they die more easily.

Final answer: Any two: delay in / lack of diagnosis; delay in / lack of treatment e.g. lack of oral rehydration therapy / clean water to make it up; lack of / less effective antibiotic therapy; antibiotic resistant strains; population malnourished / weak immune system e.g. HIV/AIDS.

hints: Recall how cholera spreads - what must happen for Vibrio from faeces to reach the mouth, and what infrastructure does an earthquake destroy?
walkthrough:
Connect Earthquake Damage to Transmission**
Cholera is transmitted by the faecal-oral route in contaminated water. An earthquake breaks sewage pipes, sewage treatment and water purification plants, and safe disposal systems. Untreated sewage then mixes with drinking water, so people ingest the bacteria and an outbreak starts.
Final answer: Earthquake damages sanitation / sewage and water purification systems, so sewage contaminates drinking water with V. cholerae, which is ingested.

hints: First separate the two y-axes: bars on the left for number of cases and line on the right for number of countries, then scan for the highest point for each.
Look at the overall direction from 2008 to 2015 for countries, and compare the shape of the bars before and after 2011.
Use the Haiti 2010 outbreak from part (c) to explain the 2011 peak and think of a reason for spread to more countries and for the later fall.
walkthrough:
Describe the 2011 Peak**
Both measures peak in 2011. Bars show number of cases rises from about 190000 in 2008 to about 590000 in 2011, then falls sharply. The line shows number of countries dips to about 48 in 2010 then jumps to the maximum of about 58 in 2011.

Explain the Peak Using Haiti**
The 2010 Haiti earthquake outbreak created an epidemic with very large case numbers reported in 2011. Spread from Haiti to neighbouring countries explains why more countries reported cholera in 2011.

Comment on the Longer Trends**
Overall the number of countries with cholera decreases from about 56 in 2008 to about 42 in 2014-2015, despite the 2011 spike. Cases increase from 2008 to 2010 while countries decrease, then after 2011 cases generally fall to a low of about 125000 in 2013. This later fall suggests improved piped treated water, sewage treatment and health education to prevent spread.

Final answer: Any three: 2011 peak / highest for both cases at approx 590000 and countries at approx 58; due to 2010 Haiti outbreak / epidemic causing high 2011 cases; spread to neighbouring countries increasing country number in 2011; overall decrease in countries from approx 56 in 2008 to approx 42 in 2015; cases rose 2008-2011 then fell, lowest cases in 2013; e.g. improved water / sewage treatment and health education reduced spread.
